market_context: United States/general English; FDA/USDA refrigeration guidance
title: How to organize your refrigerator to keep food safe longer

seo.title: How to organize your refrigerator for food safety
seo.meta_description: Keep ready-to-eat food above raw meat, raw poultry on the lowest level in leakproof containers, produce in drawers and the refrigerator at 40°F or below.
seo.search_intent: Arrange a refrigerator to reduce cross-contamination and maintain safe cold storage.

excerpt: Refrigerator organization is mainly about cold temperature and cross-contamination. Keep ready-to-eat and cooked foods above raw meat and poultry; store raw items low in leakproof containers; use produce drawers; and keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below. The door is warmer and better for less temperature-sensitive items.
content_html:
A tidy refrigerator is useful, but the real safety goal is to make it physically difficult for raw chicken juice to reach food that will be eaten without further cooking.

AreaBest use
Upper/middle shelvesCooked and ready-to-eat foods
Lowest shelfRaw meat, poultry and seafood in leakproof containers
Produce drawersFruits and vegetables
DoorLess temperature-sensitive condiments

Contain raw juices

Original meat packaging may leak. Put raw meat and poultry on a tray or in a container capable of catching liquid and keep it below ready-to-eat foods.

40°F is the important number

FDA recommends keeping the refrigerator at 40°F or below. An appliance thermometer gives more useful information than assuming a dial setting is accurate.

Do not pack so tightly that air cannot circulate

Cold air needs room to move. Overloading can create warmer pockets and make it harder for freshly stored leftovers to cool.

Use dates you can understand

Label leftovers and move older items forward. Refrigerator organization should reduce both foodborne risk and forgotten food waste.

The rule

Ready-to-eat food above, raw animal foods below, produce in drawers, and everything at 40°F or colder. Exact shelf temperatures vary by appliance, so containment and thermometer readings matter more than decorative zones.

faq.question: Where should raw chicken go in the fridge?
faq.answer: On the lowest practical shelf in a leakproof container, away from foods that will be eaten without cooking.
